# Project Plan

## Start-Up Phase

The first milestone (M1) is scheduled to begin in December 2026, following
completion of the grant agreement. I will pin versions of ten evaluation
packages, define their editing workflows, and record baseline diagnostics and
response times. I will reproduce the analysis problems described above and
document the setup so that I can compare the final results with this baseline.
Existing reproductions from `future` provide a starting point.

Initial extraction checks in September 2026 found the required fields for every
exported function in glue, withr, R6, and cli. For magrittr, coverage was 16 of
42 functions, largely because primitive aliases lack formal arguments. The
checks also found S3 methods incorrectly listed as exports. The metadata pilot
will build on these results. It will use glue, withr, R6, and cli, along with
tinytable to test a package outside the existing bundle. I will also use
magrittr to test incomplete indexes. I will fix the S3 export errors during M1,
before publication.

During M1, I will identify the overlapping code, missing APIs, and tests needed
to consolidate the readers in r-documentation-rs. I will use the pilot packages
to compare arguments, defaults, and help with results from both the existing
extractor and R, and estimate the work for M2. If full consolidation would
exceed the available hours, I will retain the parts of Arity's extractor needed
to complete the project and defer the remaining consolidation work.

Before implementation begins in M2, five pilot packages must pass the quality
criteria below. Arity must also provide signatures and help without local
installation for packages both inside and outside the existing bundle. I will
estimate the cost of weekly updates. If the pilot cannot meet these requirements
within budget, I will agree on a reduced scope with the ISC, giving priority to
the metadata features and offline access.

## Technical Delivery

  | Milestone                  | Target date       | Deliverables                                                                                 | Hours   | Cost (USD) |
  | :------------------------- | :---------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------     | ------: | ---------: |
  | M1: Baseline and pilot     | December 31, 2026 | Baseline, metadata prototype, consolidation plan, quality checks, regression cases           |      30 |      2,400 |
  | M2: Implementation         | January 31, 2027  | Reliability fixes, rich metadata publication and integration, prefetch, shared offline cache |      65 |      5,200 |
  | M3: Validation and release | February 28, 2027 | Workflow validation, annotated comparison, guides, release, report, maintenance instructions |      30 |      2,400 |
  | **Total**                  |                   |                                                                                              | **125** | **10,000** |

M1 includes planning and estimating the consolidation work. Changes to the
shared readers and their integration into Arity must fit within M2's 65 hours.
The estimates include regression tests, with eight hours in M2 set aside for
unexpected work. The project is scheduled to run from December 2026 through
February 2027. If the grant agreement is delayed, I will agree on revised
milestone dates with the ISC before work begins. I will track progress and
completion criteria in public GitHub issues.

## Other Aspects

Code and tests will use Arity's MIT license. Evaluation sources and examples
will retain applicable notices. I will publish the schema, code for the
publishing pipeline, documentation, and results, along with instructions for
rebuilding or mirroring the dataset.

Furthermore, I will invite package authors and tooling developers to try a
prerelease and will also write R Consortium blog posts to announce the project
and share results, examples, and limitations.

## Budget & Funding Plan

I intend to receive the grant personally. The requested USD 10,000 will fund 125
hours of my time at USD 80 per hour. The budget assumes no other funding or
contributors.

The dataset will be updated through GitHub actions, with snapshots on GitHub
Releases in a separate repository. I intend to maintain the pipeline after the
grant, and public scripts will let others reproduce or mirror it. I am not
requesting funds for recurring hosting costs.

With partial funding, I would publish at least 50 indexes meeting the same
quality criteria and evaluate five packages. This would still include the
metadata features and offline support described above, plus safe infix renaming.
I would defer the other reliability fixes and agree on the hours, funding, and
dates with the ISC before accepting partial funding.
